decisions.statement: Every way TypeScript names a module is read as one specifier.
A module a test replaces is named by a specifier like any other.
Every string a body has is answered too.
A specifier is a string among the strings a body spells.
What names a module is read by the same walk and answered the same way.
A specifier is answered with where the specifier is.
Specifiers are answered in the order written however deep in the body the specifiers sit.
A template is no string here.
Only a body's plain quoted text is answered.
Nothing else can be written over without reading its contents.
Where a relative specifier lands is answered as the path the specifier names and nothing more.
A specifier naming a package lands where the naming handed in says the specifier lands.
The specifier naming a path from a folder is worked out here for any caller.
A specifier spelled for a path under the folder opens with a dot and a slash.
A specifier spelled for a path outside the folder climbs to reach that path.
A path spelled as a specifier lands back on that path.
Whether a landing may be reached is not judged here.
No manifest is read here.
A caller refusing a specifier that climbs out of the root keeps that rule where the rule belongs.
Nothing here reads the disk or the index.
A specifier is the string the source says whether or not the file that specifier names is there.
The source is parsed without parent links.
A way in whose key closes with a star names every specifier opening with the part before the star.
The star is whatever the specifier has past that part however many parts that is.
Such a specifier lands where that key's target says with the star's part carried onto that target.
A way in the naming names exactly is answered before any star is tried.
A way in with no star names one specifier and nothing beneath that specifier.
A way in whose target closes with no star names no landing.
A caller handing in no naming is answered as naming no package but the root.
A specifier opening with the root package's name lands on the path that specifier names.
The root package's name is the one package name written here.
A naming naming a root specifier is answered before the root package's name.
A specifier naming a module says whether that naming is typed.
A naming TypeScript takes away before anything runs is typed, and no other is.
A module named by a call is not typed, however late that call runs.

definition: the strings a body holds, the ones naming a module, and the path tied to such a name
